chunks: And with this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a good deed is performed by eighty people, they will all be rewarded, without any decrease in the reward of any one of them.
ai.seo_question: How is reward distributed when multiple people perform a single good deed together?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses the metaphor of 'eighty hands' to illustrate that in acts of charity (Sadaqah), the reward is multiplied for every individual who contributes or facilitates the good, without diminishing the share of any other participant. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *Takaful al-Ajru* (mutual accumulation of reward), emphasizing that divine generosity does not operate on a zero-sum basis but rather expands with collective participation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 14. And from the previous chain from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
If eighty people do a good deed together each person will get the reward equal to that of all the people without decrease in the reward of any one of them.”
